title: Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin announce a "no limits" partnership in Beijing
body:
On 4 February 2022, the opening day of the Beijing Winter Olympics, Chinese President Xi Jinping hosted Russian President Vladimir Putin in Beijing. The two leaders issued a joint statement of nearly 5,400 words in English translation. It said that "friendship between the two States has no limits, there are no 'forbidden' areas of cooperation." The statement was issued about twenty days before Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

On security questions, China backed Russia's demand that Ukraine not join NATO, and both countries called for an end to NATO expansion and for security guarantees from the West. Russia had massed about 100,000 troops near Ukraine at the time, and Moscow denied planning an invasion. Russia endorsed China's position that Taiwan is an inseparable part of China and opposed any form of Taiwanese independence. Both sides also criticised the AUKUS alliance of Australia, the United Kingdom and the United States, and U.S. plans for global missile defence.

Economic agreements accompanied the statement. Gazprom and Rosneft signed new gas and oil supply deals with Beijing worth tens of billions of dollars, and Putin promoted a gas deal with China estimated at $117.5 billion. The two sides also discussed expanding trade in national currencies. The United States had diplomatically boycotted the Games. A U.S. State Department official, Daniel Kritenbrink, said Xi should have pushed for lower tensions over Ukraine.
